english.title: Shine / direct laser beam towards a land / water vehicle or aircraft
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse, shone or directed a laser beam towards a **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF VEHICLE..) which was

(A)_[moving]_
(B)_[ready to move]_

and the laser beam

(C)_[dazzled or distracted]_
(D)_[was likely to have dazzled or distracted]_

**(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a person with control of that vehicle
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1), (4) and (5) of the Laser Misuse (Vehicles) Act 2018.

english.notes:
(i) Laser beam means a beam of coherent light produced by a device of any kind (section 3 of the Laser Misuse (Vehicles) Act 2018).
(ii) Moving or ready to move is intended to capture any journey made by an aircraft, vessel or other vehicle, including land-based journeys and taxiing by aircraft and both voyages and short journeys made by vessels. It would also cover when a vehicle is about to move, and a temporary stop, such as a car stopped at traffic lights or a train stopping at a station. Subsection (6) states that a mechanically propelled vehicle which is not moving or ready to move but whose engine or motor is running, is to be treated for the purposes of Subsection (1)(a) as ready to move.
(iii) It is a defence under this section to show that either they had a reasonable excuse, or, that they did not intend to shine or direct the laser beam towards the vehicle and exercised all reasonable precautions to avoid doing so, see section 1(2) and (3) for details of this defence.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 1(4) and (5) of the Laser Misuse (Vehicles) Act 2018 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

Time limit for prosecutions:
